newsitem.title: USA: Northland Cranberries says US crop below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Northland Cranberries says US crop below estimates.

text.p: Northland Cranberries Inc said on Thursday that the total U.S. cranberry crop, including its own fruit, will fall short of August estimates.

"The small berry size we are experiencing in Wisconsin, coupled with Massachusett's inability to fully recover from last year's poor crop, suggest that the overall crop could be larger than last year, but significantly less than the record crop predicted earlier by the USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture)," John Swendrowski, president, said in a statement.
Northland said the 1996 harvest in the United States was about 50 percent complete.

In contrast with past years, Northland had not contracted to sell almost all of its fruit at fixed prices, Swendrowski said. That will allow the company to balance any shortfall in the crop with solid pricing for what fruit is harveted.
"This and other benefits of our 'marsh-to-market' strategy should become evident as fiscal 1997 unfolds, and we look forward to meeting the challenge of the coming year," he said.
Northland's marsh-to-market strategy includes growing and harvesting fruit, and selling juice products.
For the fourth quarter ended August 31, Northland reported a loss of $0.05 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.19.
For fiscal 1996, the company earned $0.50 a share, up from $0.18 a share in fiscal 1995.
Northland shares were up 2-3/8 at 17-5/8 in Nasdaq trading as of 1315 EDT/1715 GMT on Friday.
